name: grid_dipole
desc: Uniform dipole in the 3D cartesian grid format, on a posed FIELDMAP.
physics: Uniform By = 0.058218 T over 1 m. A particle entering on the axis follows a circular arc of radius 5.7588 m and leaves at 10 degrees, offset 0.087489 m. A constant field is reproduced by trilinear interpolation exactly.
checked: Bend angle and transverse offset of the reference orbit against the arc, the field window against the placement, and |p| against round-off.

name: grid_dipole_shift
desc: The same dipole map posed 0.25 m further downstream.
physics: Uniform By = 0.058218 T over 1 m. A particle entering on the axis follows a circular arc of radius 5.7588 m and leaves at 10 degrees, offset 0.087489 m. A constant field is reproduced by trilinear interpolation exactly.
checked: The field window must move by exactly 0.25 m and the bend angle must not change, which is what says the pose positions the map's own origin.

name: grid_quad
desc: Quadrupole in the 3D cartesian grid format, on a posed FIELDMAP.
physics: Quadrupole, By = g x and Bx = g y with g = 0.083816 T/m, so k1 = -0.2500 m^-2 (negative: the electron's charge makes a positive gradient defocus in x). Linear in one coordinate each, so trilinear interpolation is exact. This field is both divergence free and curl free, so its transfer matrix is symplectic.
checked: The 4x4 transverse matrix against the closed form, and its symplecticity.

name: grid_quad_2x
desc: The quadrupole map written with twice the field. The reference the two scaling cases have to match.
physics: Quadrupole, By = g x and Bx = g y with g = 0.083816 T/m, so k1 = -0.2500 m^-2 (negative: the electron's charge makes a positive gradient defocus in x). Linear in one coordinate each, so trilinear interpolation is exact. This field is both divergence free and curl free, so its transfer matrix is symplectic. Here every tabulated value is doubled.
checked: The 4x4 matrix against the closed form at twice the gradient.

name: grid_quad_scale2
desc: The plain quadrupole map with SCALE = 2 on the element.
physics: Quadrupole, By = g x and Bx = g y with g = 0.083816 T/m, so k1 = -0.2500 m^-2 (negative: the electron's charge makes a positive gradient defocus in x). Linear in one coordinate each, so trilinear interpolation is exact. This field is both divergence free and curl free, so its transfer matrix is symplectic. SCALE = 2 is applied on top.
checked: Must reproduce grid_quad_2x to round-off. That is what says SCALE is a plain multiplier on absolute Tesla rather than a normalised strength.

name: grid_quad_param
desc: The plain quadrupole field with normB = 4 and current = 2 on the param line.
physics: Quadrupole, By = g x and Bx = g y with g = 0.083816 T/m, so k1 = -0.2500 m^-2 (negative: the electron's charge makes a positive gradient defocus in x). Linear in one coordinate each, so trilinear interpolation is exact. This field is both divergence free and curl free, so its transfer matrix is symplectic. The param line asks for a factor normB/current = 2.
checked: Must reproduce grid_quad_2x to round-off. If either key were ignored the factor would come out 4 or 1/2 instead of 2.

name: grid_quad_messy
desc: The same quadrupole field written the awkward ways real files are: a comment block in front, rows out of order, nine columns.
physics: Quadrupole, By = g x and Bx = g y with g = 0.083816 T/m, so k1 = -0.2500 m^-2 (negative: the electron's charge makes a positive gradient defocus in x). Linear in one coordinate each, so trilinear interpolation is exact. This field is both divergence free and curl free, so its transfer matrix is symplectic.
checked: Must reproduce grid_quad to round-off, which is what says the comment block, the row order and the zero electric field columns make no difference.

name: grid_sol
desc: Uniform Bz in the 3D cartesian grid format, on a posed FIELDMAP.
physics: Uniform Bz = 0.1 T over 1 m, which turns the transverse momentum through k L = -0.298272 rad. There is no radial field at the ends, so this is not a focusing solenoid and not a divergence-free field; it is used because both formats carry it exactly and the motion has a closed form.
checked: The 4x4 transverse matrix against the closed form, and against the cylinder map holding the same field.

name: grid_sol_dt2
desc: grid_sol again with twice the time step, to show where the residual against the closed form comes from.
physics: Uniform Bz = 0.1 T over 1 m, which turns the transverse momentum through k L = -0.298272 rad. There is no radial field at the ends, so this is not a focusing solenoid and not a divergence-free field; it is used because both formats carry it exactly and the motion has a closed form.
checked: The residual against the closed form should be about twice grid_sol's, which is what says it is the step resolving the two hard map ends rather than a reading error.

name: cyl_sol
desc: The same uniform Bz in the 2D axisymmetric cylinder format, on a posed FIELDMAP.
physics: Uniform Bz = 0.1 T over 1 m, which turns the transverse momentum through k L = -0.298272 rad. There is no radial field at the ends, so this is not a focusing solenoid and not a divergence-free field; it is used because both formats carry it exactly and the motion has a closed form.
checked: The 4x4 matrix against the closed form, and against grid_sol: the same field in the other format has to track the same.

name: cyl_sol_solenoid
desc: The same cylinder map on a SOLENOID placed by ELEMEDGE, the other placement convention.
physics: Uniform Bz = 0.1 T over 1 m, which turns the transverse momentum through k L = -0.298272 rad. There is no radial field at the ends, so this is not a focusing solenoid and not a divergence-free field; it is used because both formats carry it exactly and the motion has a closed form.
checked: Must reproduce cyl_sol to round-off, which is what says ELEMEDGE and the pose put the map's own z = 0 at the same place, and that KS = 1 reproduces the map as written.

name: grid_efield
desc: A purely electric map in the 3D cartesian grid format, on a posed FIELDMAP.
physics: Uniform Ez = 1 MV/m over 1 m, written in the last three columns of the nine-column form. A particle crossing it gains q E dz, which for a field with no z dependence is -1.0000 MeV for this electron, whatever path it takes. Constant, so trilinear interpolation is exact.
checked: The energy the reference particle gains against q E dz, which is what says the electric columns are read, converted from MV/m to V/m, and actually applied.

name: grid_efield_escale2
desc: The same electric map with ESCALE = 2 on the element.
physics: Uniform Ez = 1 MV/m over 1 m, written in the last three columns of the nine-column form. A particle crossing it gains q E dz, which for a field with no z dependence is -1.0000 MeV for this electron, whatever path it takes. Constant, so trilinear interpolation is exact. ESCALE = 2 is applied on top.
checked: The energy change must be exactly twice grid_efield's, which is what says ESCALE is a plain multiplier on the tabulated field.

name: grid_eb
desc: Electric and magnetic field in one map, both switched on.
physics: Uniform Ez = 1 MV/m over 1 m, written in the last three columns of the nine-column form. A particle crossing it gains q E dz, which for a field with no z dependence is -1.0000 MeV for this electron, whatever path it takes. Constant, so trilinear interpolation is exact. The same map also carries the uniform dipole By, so the particle is bent and changes energy at the same time.
checked: The energy change still matches q E dz even though the orbit is bent, because the work only depends on the z crossed.

name: grid_eb_bonly
desc: The same combined map with ESCALE = 0, so only the magnetic half acts.
physics: Uniform Ez = 1 MV/m over 1 m, written in the last three columns of the nine-column form. A particle crossing it gains q E dz, which for a field with no z dependence is -1.0000 MeV for this electron, whatever path it takes. Constant, so trilinear interpolation is exact. Here ESCALE = 0 switches the electric field off entirely.
checked: Must reproduce grid_dipole to round-off. That is the sharp test that the two scales are independent: the same file, one field switched off, has to track like the magnet-only map.

name: cyl_ramp
desc: The asymmetric solenoid profile, read the way it is written.
physics: A solenoid profile that is deliberately not symmetric in z, with the radial field from the usual first-order expansion. Turning it round is a different field, which is what makes it a fair test of ZREVERSE.
checked: Provides the field profile the reversed cases are compared with; its own field window and |p| are checked.

name: cyl_ramp_zrev
desc: The same map with ZREVERSE = TRUE, which turns the magnet round.
physics: A solenoid profile that is deliberately not symmetric in z, with the radial field from the usual first-order expansion. Turning it round is a different field, which is what makes it a fair test of ZREVERSE.
checked: Must reproduce cyl_ramp_mirror to round-off, and must differ from cyl_ramp -- otherwise the profile was symmetric and the test would prove nothing.

name: cyl_ramp_mirror
desc: The mirrored field written out as its own map file: z reflected and Bz negated, Br left alone.
physics: A solenoid profile that is deliberately not symmetric in z, with the radial field from the usual first-order expansion. Turning it round is a different field, which is what makes it a fair test of ZREVERSE. Written out already turned round.
checked: The reference cyl_ramp_zrev is compared with.
